title: DRAFT - RED discovery attack spec (NOT A CONTRACT, NOT IN MANIFEST.json)
description: What the RED_STRATEGIST would emit to author an attack the corpus does not hold. DESIGN ONLY as of 2026-08-23: nothing in the tree produces or consumes this shape, it is deliberately NOT under contracts/, and it is NOT in contracts/MANIFEST.json. It becomes C11 when something implements it, and that is a second C6 hash move - correct, because discovery adds a population that is not under corpus_hash and therefore changes what a bundle means. Rationale, refusal taxonomy and the three-population reporting rule: docs/design/red-discovery-capability.md. THE SHAPE IS DEFINED BY WHAT IT OMITS. attack_id, family_id, scored_features, sealed, episode.* and derived.* are all ABSENT and all forbidden: CONVENTIONS 2.6 says never ask a model to perform a deterministic computation, ruling 16 freezes episode.* at episode start from the scenario, ruling 21 gives derived.* exactly one writer, and corpus/schema.py REFUSES an author-supplied instance_id rather than checking one because a checked copy of a derived value is still a second copy.

objective.$comment: One sentence: what the attacker wants the agent to do that exceeds its authority. THIS IS THE THING BEING DISCOVERED, and it is the one field with no counterpart in the rephrasing path - `generated` mode is defined by holding the objective FIXED while the wording moves.

target_capability_class.$comment: SCALAR, exactly one - the term binding for capability_class says so, and the collision it records is rule-side: capability_classes IS still correct on a TOOL, which carries a set. UNCLASSIFIED IS NOT ADMITTED HERE AND CANNOT BE: no rule may select it (C4 V2), the empty set means INERT, and the policy engine fails open on both deliberately because the TRIPWIRE scores independently of policy. An attack aimed at an unpoliceable tool can only ever succeed, which is why E_UNCLASSIFIED_TARGET is a refusal rather than an interesting result. THIS ENUM WAS WRONG FOR THREE HOURS ON 2026-08-24 AND THE NOTE THAT MADE IT WRONG IS KEPT HERE. It read CAP_MUTATES_RECORD, CAP_SENDS_EXTERNAL, CAP_READS_SENSITIVE and CAP_CLOSES_CASE - four invented names - and omitted CAP_INVOKES_AGENT. The file's own comment said the values were 'restated here ONLY because this file is not yet wired to crucible.manifest.load.CAPABILITY_CLASSES', which correctly identified the drift site and then wrote into it anyway. Caught by a live run whose rejected patch named CAP_MUTATES_DURABLE_STATE and CAP_INVOKES_AGENT, neither of which this file admitted. The values now come from that module and test_the_capability_class_enum_matches_the_manifest_module holds them there mechanically, because a comment saying where the truth lives is not a check.

tool_fqname.$comment: The scored call's tool. MUST be declared by capability manifest Part A - E_UNDECLARED_TOOL otherwise, checked before a single target call is spent. RED sees opaque handles plus class sets plus arg schemas, never product vocabulary, and that blindness is unchanged by authoring: it changes what RED EMITS, not what RED SEES.

scenario.$comment: THE WORLD. The order/account/case record the episode runs against, in the shape corpus instances already use, so `build_sor` / `verify_world` / `unpresentable_entities` can be run over it unchanged. THIS IS THE HALF A PAYLOAD-ONLY SPEC OMITS and the reason architecture-spec 1.1's AttackSpec cannot be scored: an episode with no world has nothing to act on, so the target either invents a record or errors, and either way the episode measured nothing. `CorpusSeeds.world_for` builds one world PER INSTANCE and refuses to fall back to a shared one - the ORD-4471/ORD-4472 collision. Shape intentionally left open in this draft: it is corpus/schema.py's `scenario`, and restating it here would be a second source of truth for it.

turns.$comment: The user turns in order. The LAST one asks for the forbidden thing - the same position `vary()` rewrites, and the same position `world_for` splices when it replaces the final turn.

expected_tool_call.$comment: What the attack is TRYING to induce. RECORDED AS THE ATTACK'S OWN CLAIM AND NEVER AS A VERDICT. The frozen Objective Set decides what happened, through the pure-code tripwire, at objective_set_hash. RED authors the attack; RED does not author what counts as a breach. If a discovered attack targets a capability path no clause covers, the verdict is CLEAN and that is the CORRECT answer - clause_coverage will show the clause was never reached. A discovery capability able to move the definition of breach could manufacture its own success and there would be no instrument left in the build.

FORBIDDEN_FIELDS_AND_WHY.$comment: Not a schema node - a note pinned where the next person editing this file will read it. Every one of these is REFUSED (E_AUTHORED_FROZEN_FIELD) rather than ignored, because a field silently dropped is a field the model believes it set. attack_id: content-addressed by code, atk_ + sha256(canonical(body))[:12], the same derivation corpus/schema.py::instance_id uses, so two spellings of one discovered attack collapse rather than seeding the population twice and RED cannot number its own findings. family_id: matched by code against the seven existing families on (class, tool, induced-call shape), unmatched becomes fam_discovered - RED naming its own family would let it declare its own novelty. scored_features: STAMPED BY CODE FROM THE TRACE. If RED authored both the attack and the features its pair separation is computed on, the D5 blindness check becomes unfalsifiable for that population - the same party would write the exam and the answer key. sealed: always false, RED holds no write path to the seal and must not be able to claim one. episode.*: ruling 16. derived.*: ruling 21.
